title: English river invertebrate richness stopped rising after about 2001, but communities kept shifting to pollution-sensitive families to 2017 at 23,600 sites; autumn gains stopped in 2018-2025
abstract: We tested if the plateau in English river invertebrate richness means that recovery from organic pollution stopped. We used Environment Agency kick samples: ChemPop (1,515 long-term sites, 1989-2017, with water quality, air temperature and flow) and the EA open data release of 2026-11-10 (201,155 samples at 23,604 sites, 1989-2025), which gave independent sites and the independent period 2018-2025. We harmonised family labels between the two taxonomies and split 100 core families into ammonia-sensitive, middle and tolerant thirds with cross-fitted 1989-1995 associations. The external WHPT ASPT index was a check. Models compared each site with itself and removed sampling day and recording method. Within-site richness rose by 0.42 families per year until a break in 2001-2002 and then stopped (autumn -0.043 per year, 95% CI -0.079 to -0.012). In 2005-2017 composition kept changing: sensitive families rose by +0.072 to +0.089 per year, tolerant families fell by -0.067 to -0.069 per year, and WHPT ASPT rose by +0.019 to +0.021 per year, about half the 1989-2004 rate. WHPT ASPT and a community ammonia index moved toward clean-water communities in all 28 region, season and site-set tests, also with log-category records only, a fixed-site panel and central sampling dates. Sites in the most polluted ammonia third in 2003-06 still gained 0.9-1.2 families by 2014-17, while the cleanest third lost families. Temperature and flow changes gave no clear offset. In 2018-2025, richness fell in autumn (-0.155 per year, CI -0.238 to -0.053), tolerant families kept falling, and autumn sensitive-family and WHPT ASPT gains stopped; spring ASPT gains continued. In a post-hoc regional test, warm summers lowered autumn ASPT (-0.040 per 1 C), but the warmer, drier summers of 2018-2025 predicted a small richness gain, not the observed loss. Thus richness stopped rising because tolerant losses cancelled sensitive gains, not because recovery stopped. The cause of the 2018-2025 autumn stall is open. Limits: associations only; tolerance groups come from the same source (external index agrees); no water-quality data after 2017; England only.

citations.reason: Reports that European freshwater invertebrate recovery came to a halt; we show that in England richness stopped but composition kept recovering to 2017, while autumn gains stopped after 2018.
Reported that English river richness recovery slowed after about 2003; our break analysis agrees (break 1997-2002).
ChemPop v2.0 source data (OGL v3): macroinvertebrates with matched water quality, air temperature and flow, 1989-2017.
EA Ecology & Fish Data Explorer INV_OPEN_DATA and OPEN_DATA_TAXON_INFO, release file 2026-11-10 (OGL v3): independent sites, 2018-2025 and WHPT ASPT.
Met Office HadUK-Grid regional seasonal temperature and rainfall (OGL v3) for the post-hoc climate test.
We reuse its loading code, fixed-effects solver and core-family approach; it noted the richness plateau after 2005 that we test here.
Found weak local but full mean transfer of pollution-score change in the same source; our window regressions also show that local water-quality change explains little of the mean change.
